## Solution

The two circles $|z|=1$ and $|z-1|=1$ meet at the two points
$$z = \tfrac{1}{2} \pm \tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i = e^{\pm i\pi/3}.$$
The region to be mapped is the lens (lune) bounded by the two circular arcs joining these points.

**Step 1 — Send the two vertices to $0$ and $\infty$.** Both boundary circles pass through $e^{\pm i\pi/3}$, so the Möbius transformation
$$w_1 = \frac{z - e^{i\pi/3}}{z - e^{-i\pi/3}}$$
maps each boundary circle to a straight line through the origin. The lens region is therefore mapped to a sector.

**Step 2 — Identify the sector.** Evaluate $w_1$ at a convenient point of each boundary:
- On $|z|=1$, take $z=0$: $\;w_1(0) = \dfrac{-e^{i\pi/3}}{-e^{-i\pi/3}} = e^{i2\pi/3}$, so this boundary is the ray $\arg w_1 = 2\pi/3$.
- On $|z-1|=1$, take $z=1$: $\;1-e^{i\pi/3}=e^{-i\pi/3},\; 1-e^{-i\pi/3}=e^{i\pi/3}$, so $w_1(1)=e^{-i2\pi/3}$, giving the ray $\arg w_1 = -2\pi/3\;(=4\pi/3)$.

An interior point, say $z=\tfrac12$, gives $w_1(\tfrac12)=\dfrac{-i\sqrt3/2}{i\sqrt3/2}=-1=e^{i\pi}$, which lies between the two rays going through $\pi$. Hence the lens maps to the sector
$$\frac{2\pi}{3} < \arg w_1 < \frac{4\pi}{3}, \qquad \text{opening angle } \frac{2\pi}{3}.$$

**Step 3 — Rotate the sector to the standard position.** Multiply by $e^{-i2\pi/3}$:
$$\zeta = e^{-i2\pi/3}\,w_1 = e^{-i2\pi/3}\,\frac{z-e^{i\pi/3}}{z-e^{-i\pi/3}},$$
which sends the sector to $0 < \arg\zeta < 2\pi/3$.

**Step 4 — Open the sector to a half-plane.** Raising to the power $\pi/(2\pi/3)=3/2$ (using the branch $\arg\zeta\in[0,2\pi/3]\subset(-\pi,\pi]$, so the branch cut along the negative real axis does not meet the sector):
$$w_2 = \zeta^{3/2} = \left(e^{-i2\pi/3}\,\frac{z-e^{i\pi/3}}{z-e^{-i\pi/3}}\right)^{3/2}.$$
This maps the sector $0<\arg\zeta<2\pi/3$ conformally onto the upper half-plane $\operatorname{Im} w_2 > 0$.

**Step 5 — Map the upper half-plane to the unit disk.** The Cayley transform
$$W = \frac{w_2 - i}{w_2 + i}$$
maps $\operatorname{Im} w_2 > 0$ onto $|W|<1$.

**Verification.** Composing, the required conformal mapping is
$$\boxed{\;W = \frac{\displaystyle\left(e^{-2\pi i/3}\,\frac{z-e^{i\pi/3}}{z-e^{-i\pi/3}}\right)^{3/2}-i}{\displaystyle\left(e^{-2\pi i/3}\,\frac{z-e^{i\pi/3}}{z-e^{-i\pi/3}}\right)^{3/2}+i}\;}$$

Checking key points:
- $z=\tfrac12$ (center of the lens): $\zeta = e^{-i2\pi/3}(-1)=e^{i\pi/3}$, $w_2=(e^{i\pi/3})^{3/2}=e^{i\pi/2}=i$, $W=(i-i)/(i+i)=0$. ✓ The lens center maps to the disk center.
- $z=0$ (on $|z|=1$): $\zeta=1$, $w_2=1$, $W=(1-i)/(1+i)=-i$, $|W|=1$. ✓ Boundary maps to boundary.
- $z=1$ (on $|z-1|=1$): $\zeta=e^{i2\pi/3}$, $w_2=(e^{i2\pi/3})^{3/2}=e^{i\pi}=-1$, $W=(-1-i)/(-1+i)$, $|W|=1$. ✓

Each stage is conformal and one-to-one on the relevant region (Möbius maps are globally conformal; the power $3/2$ is conformal on the sector since the sector opening $2\pi/3<2\pi$ and avoids the branch cut; the Cayley map is conformal on the half-plane). The composition is therefore a conformal bijection from the lens $\{|z|<1\}\cap\{|z-1|<1\}$ onto the unit disk $|W|<1$.
